name: Felix
summary: The governor to whom Paul was sent as a prisoner at Caesarea. He heard Paul speak and trembled, but he put off his decision and left Paul bound for two years.

key_moments.title: Receives Paul as a Prisoner
key_moments.description: Under heavy guard, Paul was taken by night to Caesarea with a letter for Felix the governor. Felix read it, said he would hear Paul when his accusers came, and had him kept in Herod's judgment hall.

key_moments.title: Hearing Both Sides
key_moments.description: Tertullus accused Paul before Felix, and Paul denied their charges. Felix, who knew about the Way, put off his decision and kept Paul under guard but let him have some freedom.

key_moments.title: Trembles at Paul's Words
key_moments.description: Felix and his wife Drusilla sent for Paul to hear about faith in Christ. As Paul spoke of right living, self-control and the judgment ahead, Felix was afraid and sent him away. He hoped Paul would pay him money, and after two years he left Paul bound to please the Jews.
